clue.text: Hardy partner's won the honours

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the comic partner of Oliver Hardy
the possessive ending supplies its letter S

explanation.surface: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner has scooped the awards.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were a classic film comedy double act; the possessive gives the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurel wreaths were awarded to victors, so the word stands for distinctions or accolades.

clue.text: Try reversing? That's crazy!

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the word for try backwards

parts.note: to have a stab at something is to try it

explanation.surface: Someone protests that attempting to go backwards is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone off their head is said to be bats.

clue.text: Scold soldiers in a Spanish port

indicators.note: in places the soldiers within the name of the port

parts.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, north-west Spain
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A nagging woman berates troops stationed in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, bad-tempered woman, a shrew who rails at others.

clue.text: Thousands staked by one of the family

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
money staked on a horse is said to be on it

explanation.surface: A gambler bets thousands, and he is a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's son is a relative, a member of the family line.

clue.text: Fly Tory needs courage

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, so a Tory is a blue
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician must be brave to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A large buzzing blowfly is a common household insect of this name.

clue.text: Porridge makes a good man want to be sick

parts.note: ST, for saint, is a good man in crossword convention
to retch is to heave as if about to vomit

explanation.surface: Breakfast oats leave a virtuous man feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, not oats here; ST is the usual abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a term served in prison.

clue.text: Fever contracted by a dire liar in Morocco

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters within the country code

parts.note: MA is the international vehicle code for Morocco

indicators.note: dire suggests the letters are in a terrible state, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tropical illness was caught from a terrible fibber in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito-borne disease whose main symptom is recurring bouts of high temperature.

clue.text: High churchman makes priest cheer

parts.note: to elate is to cheer or delight

explanation.surface: A senior cleric bucks up a parish clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or archbishop is a senior member of the clergy, high in rank.

clue.text: Drove one crazy by being mawkish

parts.note: drove in the sense of sent someone, as in drove him mad
I is the Roman numeral one
mental is informal for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone was driven mad by sloppy, soppy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe excessive, cloying emotion or sickly nostalgia.

clue.text: Piece of bread one served with an aquatic delicacy

parts.note: a crust is a piece of bread
an ace in tennis is a serve that wins the point outright

explanation.surface: A diner is given a slice of bread with a seafood treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobster, crab and prawns belong to this shellfish class and are prized eating.

clue.text: Some achieve real success all the time

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people achieve genuine success all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always or at all times, as in ever-present.

clue.text: Faint radio signal has clearly been lost

definitions.text: radio signal has clearly been lost

explanation.surface: A weak radio broadcast seems to have disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary loss of consciousness, and also a total cut in communications or broadcasts.

clue.text: Barrister went ahead and gave advice

parts.note: counsel is a barrister conducting a case in court
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A lawyer took the lead and offered guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to guide or recommend a course to them.

clue.text: Tax church north of the border

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: A church levy is collected in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: North of the border, from an English point of view, means in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Here an adjective for things from Scotland, which lies beyond England's northern frontier.

clue.text: Only a very little wait!

parts.note: just means only or merely
minute means tiny

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a moment's patience, only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A common spoken idiom asking someone to hold on for a moment.

clue.text: Gossips left in ragged clothing

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left within the word for rags

parts.note: tatters are torn, ragged clothes

explanation.surface: Chattering neighbours were left wearing rags.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who tell tales or chatter idly about others are telltales.

clue.text: Officer awards pass to ace trainee

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
an ace counts as one in cards
L, for learner, marks a trainee driver

explanation.surface: A commanding officer hands top marks to a promising cadet.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on a British trainee driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: An army rank above lieutenant colonel and below brigadier.

clue.text: He reads riot act after being fleeced

indicators.note: a riot suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged in a wild act

explanation.surface: A man lays down the law after being swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleeced looks like cheated, but here it is what is done to sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A shorn sheep has had its wool coat removed.

clue.text: Businesses prepared to offer tlc

parts.note: COS is the plural abbreviation of company
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: Companies are ready to give loving care to their staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper or mollycoddle someone is to give them tender loving care.

clue.text: Capital Henry invested in modern food shop

parts.note: new means modern

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the shop

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry has put money into a trendy grocery business.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of India's government, so it is that nation's capital city.

clue.text: A ponderous mass as part of address for Kensington palace

parts.words: part of address for Kensington palace
parts.note: Kensington Palace in London has the postcode W8, whose letter W comes first

parts.words: part of address for Kensington palace
parts.note: the number in the W8 postcode, written out as a word

explanation.surface: A heavy lump forms part of a royal residence's address.
explanation.walkthrough: British postcodes begin with a district code; Kensington Palace's is W8, and writing the 8 as a word gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy load is a burden of great heft, something hefty to lift.

clue.text: Utterly disgusting poultry

indicators.note: Utterly signals something uttered, so the word is spoken

parts.note: foul means disgusting

explanation.surface: Some chicken is completely revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic birds such as chickens and ducks reared for eggs or meat.

clue.text: Maligned an unusually important player

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A star actor is unusually slandered.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor taking the principal male role in a play or film.

clue.text: It takes courage to bare their bellies

definitions.text: It takes courage to bare their bellies

parts.words: It takes courage to bare their bellies
parts.note: one word means both nerve and belly, so showing your stomach takes nerve

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for bravery, and also the abdomen or innards.

clue.text: High jinks in bar backing on to railway

indicators.note: backing means the word for bar is read backwards

parts.note: a lever is a bar used for prising

explanation.surface: Wild partying happens in a pub next to the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar suggests a pub but is the crowbar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous merrymaking or partying, lively fun.

clue.text: One alternative is to stimulate the woman

parts.note: to whet is to sharpen or stimulate, as with an appetite
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: One option is to arouse the lady's interest.
explanation.definitionFit: This conjunction introduces a choice between possibilities, as in or not.
